titles.entity_title: Spygate: Eckert free to continue as Southampton manager

synopses.short: John Bennett is joined by Adam Blackmore and Jobi McAnuff to react to the Spygate verdict
synopses.medium: John Bennett is joined by BBC Radio Solent's Adam Blackmore and the 72+ podcast's Jobi McAnuff to react to the Spygate verdict.
synopses.long:
John Bennett is joined by BBC Radio Solent's Adam Blackmore and former Reading and Watford winger Jobi McAnuff to react to the Spygate verdict. 

An FA regulatory commission has handed Southampton boss Tonda Eckert a suspended 6-week ban for his involvement in the Spygate scandal. What reasons were given for this verdict? And is it a fair outcome? 

With Middlesborough the club to uncover the spying ahead of their Championship play-off semi-final,  fan and editor of Fly Me To The Moon fanzine, Robert Nichols, offers what this decision is like from a Boro perspective. 

TIMECODES:
0'45 How did we get to this point? 
2'05 Why is the ban suspended?
4'17 Jobi McAnuff's thoughts
9'12 Has the length of time taken to get this verdict benefitted Eckert? 
11'51 What do Southampton fans think of the decision? 
15'00 Middlesborough fan Robert Nichols
18'05 How much damage has this done to Southampton's reputation?

titles.secondary: Does Pocognoli need to change already?
titles.entity_title: Does Pocognoli need to change already?

synopses.short: Scotland slump to Slovenia: is Pocognoli's back three already in trouble?
synopses.medium: Scotland fall 2-1 to Slovenia at Hampden. Is Pocognoli's system wrong for his players? Plus Bowie, Gannon-Doak, Angus Gunn and O'Neill staying at Celtic.
synopses.long:
What should we make of Scotland's slump to defeat against Slovenia at Hampden? Four games into Pocognoli's time in charge, how clear is his project, and is the back three the right fit for the players he has? With second place in the Nations League group now looking a long way off, is it time to go back to the drawing board?

Martin Dowden, Steven McGowan and Cammy Bell look at a flat night at Hampden. Scotland took the lead but deserved to lose. The panel looks at a press that never worked as one unit, a high line that kept getting broken by a single ball over the top, and centre-backs Stephen Welsh, Jack Hendry and Binks being left exposed one-on-one. They also discuss three formation changes in one game, Andy Robertson asking the touchline what to do, and whether Slovenia had studied Scotland's last few games. Plus, is a 4-2-3-1 the answer, and is Steve Clarke now looking a little better in hindsight?

Plus, should Kieran Bowie have started after scoring against North Macedonia? Has Ollie McBurnie's run without a goal gone on too long? How can Scotland get the best out of Ben Gannon-Doak while he isn't playing at Bournemouth? Is the criticism of Angus Gunn fair, or does the trouble start well before the ball reaches him? Do Josh McPake, James Wilson and the under-21s give Scotland real depth?

And with Martin O'Neill committing to stay as Celtic manager, can he get through Motherwell, Benfica, Hearts and Celta Vigo with his critics quiet?

titles.secondary: Could Royal Oak FC End Up Playing Man City?!
titles.entity_title: Could Royal Oak FC End Up Playing Man City?!

synopses.short: Royal Oak FC finally win, Man City are found guilty and Andy Townsend talks pub toilets.
synopses.medium: Royal Oak FC finally win, Parksey wants a subs deduction, and the lads react to Man City's guilty verdict.
synopses.long:
It's been a monumental week in football, as Royal Oak FC have finally won a game! Buoyed by their recent clear-the-air talks and Steve's trip to Turkey, their fortunes are on the up.

The only cloud on the horizon is Parksey, who went off at half-time (he's asked for a pro-rata deduction in his subs), while the lads discuss his future role at the club.

In the wider football world, the lads drill down into the breaking news that Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules. Steve, Paul and Bob take a fan's-eye view of the fallout.

Elsewhere, Andy Townsend weighs in on pub toilets, and the lads ponder whose life they'd most like to live as a footballer.

Erling Haaland, José Mourinho and Hakan Şükür all feature in another packed edition.

You can also watch the YouTube premiere of each episode on the Game’s Gone channel, every Thursday at 7pm with Bob and Steve in the live chat.

Send your questions and voice notes to steve@bbc.co.uk or via whatsapp 0800 7831997

Marching on, together as one. Steve.

synopses.short: Ellen White sits down with defender Esme Morgan ahead of England's World Cup qualifiers.
synopses.long:
Ellen White is back at St. George’s Park, alongside BBC Women's Sport Reporter Jo Currie, for a Lionesses special ahead of their upcoming World Cup play-off games against Greece.

Ellen sits down with Washington Spirit defender Esme Morgan to discuss finding consistency in the England starting XI, how the NWSL season has prepared her for these crucial international games, and we of course get an update on Biscuit the cat!

Plus, Jo chats to England’s exciting new midfield talents in the press conference, Lexi Potter and Erica Meg Parkinson. 

Full commentary of England v Greece is on BBC Radio 5 Live and BBC Sounds. The first leg is a 5:30pm kick-off on Friday 9th October.

container.title: Football on Trial: The Manchester City Charges

synopses.short: Clive Myrie tells the football story of the century: the Premier League vs Man City.
synopses.medium: Clive Myrie tells the football story of the century: the Premier League vs Man City.
synopses.long:
Eight Premier League titles. Six League Cups. Three FA Cups. The Champions League. Since an extraordinary takeover in 2008, Manchester City have become one of the most dominant football clubs in the world. 

But what did it take to get there? 

Clive Myrie tells the inside story of the rise of Manchester City and the Premier League allegations of financial rule-breaking that threaten to put an asterisk next to their accolades and throw English football into disarray. 

Over four episodes you will hear from those who were there when Manchester City went from being a one-stop soap opera to Premier League domination to a potentially catastrophic censure. 

Subscribe now so you don't miss further reactive episodes presented by Clive Myrie where he will break down a verdict that could change English football forever.
